newsitem.title: USA: Marine Drilling shares rise on WAPET contracts.
newsitem.headline: Marine Drilling shares rise on WAPET contracts.

text.p: Marine Drilling Cos Inc shares rose 2-1/8, 10.83 percent, to 21-3/4 after the company announced it had been awarded a contract by a group of companies lead by West Australian Petroleum Pty. Limited (WAPET).
"The contract is currently projected to commence on or before January 1, 1999 and is expected to produce total revenues of $164 million to $188 million," Marine said in a statement.

Drilling will take place in the Pacific Rim, Southeast Asia, offshore Australia and New Zealand. The day rate will be adjusted for each operating area to compensate for the respective expenses incurred in each area, the company said.
Marine said its Marine 500 second-generation semi-submersible, will be upgraded for the contract to work in water depths up to 5,000 feet with 15,000 pounds per square inch drilling equipment.
WAPET is the operator of a joint venture between Chevron Corp, Texaco Inc, Royal Dutch/Shell and Mobil Corp.
